newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends firm, Skikda muddies the waters.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends firm, Skikda muddies the waters.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended modestly higher on Tuesday after continued delays at Algeria's Skikda port muddied the waters for traders counting up cargoes and gauging demand for December.
Crude's recent gallop higher also buoyed naphtha.

One end-user was shipping material from Tunisia to Antwerp because of the Skikda delays and another was a noted buyer over the last week, which some traders speculated was to buy time to meet prompt demand in NWE.
Glencore fixed the World Prophet tanker for 26,000 tonnes of naphtha for loading December 12 out of Bizerta, Tunisia, to the Med, according to shipping sources.
The World Prophet was also fixed for loading of 27,000 tonnes on December 12 out of Skikda to either the Med or NWE, the sources said.

But market sources questioned what impact the Skikda delays was having on prices and said it may not be known until the port reopens and the four cargoes waiting to be loaded eventually reach their homes.
Two cargoes were already expected to go to Brazil and the U.S. but the other two were of keen interest in case another heads across the Atlantic after recent arbitrage interest.

"I think naphtha is extremely expensive from a crack point of view," said one trader, who said the naphtha to crude crack spread was at a rich $55 a tonne. "Naphtha is still expensive with no demand."
A 6,000 tonne Russian cargo was still seen on offer in NWE at $233 cif with the most recent bid at $225.
One trader said there was difficulty in selling the cargo due to the high price and the poor quality, which is low paraffinic and must be blended with paraffinic material.
He also said there was Scandinavian material available in NWE offered at high quotes plus $3-$4.
A bid for piepeline spec material for delivery by Dec 15 was last at $231 cif after reaching as high as $232, with the offer at $234, said one source.
Trading in heavier N+A material was still seen lacklustre due to very weak reformer margins.
A port official said a methane carrier may be berthed on Tuesday afternoon at Skikda and oil tankers may be able to berth on Wednesday, based on improved weather forecasts.
